title: Comparison of plant feedstocks and methods to recover leaf proteins from wet fractionation of alfalfa for potential use in aquaculture, poultry, and livestock feeds
geography: Waseca, Minnesota, United States; plots at the University of Minnesota Southern Research and Outreach Center
material_scope: UMN4624 biomass-type alfalfa herbage and press filtrate; values here are from the recovery-method comparison
source_location: Table 5 and Section 2.3, APC recovery methods
license: Article is labelled Open Access on publisher page; specific reuse license subtype not identified in the accessible article text.
data_handling: Transcribed Table 5 means and Fisher protected LSD significance letters. APC recovery is g APC per kg herbage on a dry-matter basis. Product composition is g constituent per kg APC. Limiting amino acids is the combined methionine, lysine and threonine concentration. The methods comparison used three replications. Treatment conditions are from Table 5 footnotes; the herbage was harvested at about 50% flowering on 13 September 2016 and sample handling is described in Section 2.3.
uncertainty: n=3; table presents significance groups but no numeric SEM, SD, or confidence intervals for the Table 5 outcomes.
limitations: Alfalfa is not roadside grass; the data are not transferable as a GreenHub default or direct roadside-grass performance estimate.
The experimental preparation and press-filtrate composition differ from the GreenHub route; processing used homogenization with deionized water and hand pressing through cheesecloth.
Acid and base solution concentrations and pH endpoints are reported, but reagent volume or mass dose is not; pH endpoint alone does not determine titration demand.
APC mass recovery is not equivalent to true-protein recovery from incoming feed protein; the reported APC also contains fat, sugars, fiber, and other constituents.
No continuous process energy, equipment scale, separator performance, or economic data are inferred from this table.
